$comment: v1.1 — frozen per docs/14-implementation-plan-ph5.md Step 3 (R2), same discipline as finding.schema.json (Step 2's A3): publish before an external MCP client depends on the shape. Mirrors pkg/recon.ReconResult exactly. confidence values here ("high"|"medium"|"low") mirror pkg/agenttask.Confidence's band convention, NOT Finding.confidence (a distinct, detector-set, two-value field) — docs/91-research-recon-phase.md already corrected this exact conflation once. v1.1 (Step 3b): TechFact.host added as required — R8's decision engine needs to know which host produced a tech signal to set a PlanTree leaf's Target; a real omission in v1, corrected before Phase 6's MCP server (the only planned external consumer) exists. v1.2 (Phase 6 Step 3, D2): optional `policy` object added — Wave 0's fetched security.txt/robots.txt signals, input to the pkg/preflight program-policy pre-flight check; a backward-compatible additive field, absent unless Wave 0 found something. v1.3 (demo batch, LT-30b): EndpointFact gains optional `body_len`/`content_type`/`title` — response-shape signal probeCommonPaths/httpx measure, so a downstream soft-404/SPA-catch-all check can tell a real distinct resource from a shell served for every path; all additive, omitted when unmeasured. v1.4 (Phase 7 Step 4, D6): optional `uniform_response` object — set by Wave 3 when a host answers every probe with one generic page (a WAF/bot/auth block wall or a SPA/bucket catch-all), consumed by the decision engine (LT-58) and the scan engine's corpus short-circuit (LT-59); additive, absent on a normally-routing host. v1.5 (near-term batch, LT-68): optional `app_surface` object — recon's synthesised none/thin/full verdict on whether there is a live application worth planning against; additive, `plan`/`scan` echo it to stderr. v1.6 (Phase 8 Step 6, LT-64): EndpointFact gains optional `redirect_chain`/`final_url` — set only when httpx followed a redirect to a different host; `status_code` is then the first-hop 3xx, and body_len/content_type/title/tech are omitted, so a cross-host redirect isn't recorded as the target's own 200. Additive, absent on the common no-cross-host-redirect case. v1.7 (Phase 8 Step 6 second tranche, LT-40): a new EndpointFact `source` value `"api-spec"` — routes walked out of a reachable OpenAPI/Swagger JSON document (`paths`/`parameters`), path templating kept verbatim (`/users/{id}`) and documented query keys appended keyless; no schema-shape change (source is a free-form string). LT-61 adds a `cdn-edge:` line to a HostFact's `notes` when the host's ASN is a known CDN edge network — also no shape change. v1.8 (Phase 8 Step 6, LT-90): EndpointFact gains optional `auth_required` — a boolean set only on a `source: "api-spec"` fact when the OpenAPI document declares the route needs authentication; the decision engine turns a parameterless auth-required spec route into an authbypass candidate. Additive, absent/false otherwise. v1.9 (Phase 8 Step 3): a new top-level `secrets` array — hardcoded-secret hits (AWS/Google/Slack/GitHub keys, private-key headers, hardcoded Bearer tokens) found by static analysis of Wave 3's already-fetched JS bodies. Each entry carries only a redacted match, never the real secret value. Additive, empty/absent when nothing was found. Also new EndpointFact `source` values `"js-static"` (LinkFinder-style endpoint extraction from JS bodies) and `"js-static-cloud"` (an AWS S3 / GCS bucket URL shape found in JS or already-crawled endpoints) and new TechFact `name` values `"aws"`/`"s3"`/`"gcp"` (cloud-provider fingerprinting) — no schema-shape change, both fields already accept free-form strings. v1.10 (LT-96): EndpointFact gains optional `body_param_keys` — a `source: "api-spec"` fact's requestBody JSON schema property names, feeding SuggestSSRFBodyParamsFromRecon for a target that takes an attacker-controlled URL in a JSON body field rather than a query string. Additive, absent when the operation has no requestBody or wasn't spec-derived. v1.11 (Part B, --auto-provision-account): a new top-level `signup_endpoint` object — a candidate account-registration route, presence/shape-only like `api_spec` (recon never confirms the route actually creates an account). Set either from an OpenAPI operation whose operationId/summary names it as a signup route, or, when no spec is available, a path-guess probe against a curated candidate list. Consumed by pkg/provision (never by recon itself, which stays read/enumerate-only). Additive, absent when recon found no candidate. v1.12 (LT-135): a new top-level `coupon_endpoint` object — a candidate coupon/promo mint+apply endpoint pair, carrying real request-body field names alongside the paths (reusing `body_param_keys`' schema-extraction machinery, LT-96) so pkg/detectors/businesslogic isn't limited to crAPI's own field names either. Spec-derived only, deliberately no path-guess fallback (a mint endpoint is POST-only and mutating, so recon never probes for one — unlike signup_endpoint's GET-safe path guess). Additive, absent when no spec documented a coupon-shaped pair. v1.13 (LT-140): `uniform_response` (a single nullable object, first-host-wins) replaced by `uniform_responses` (an array, one entry per walled host) — the one first-writer-wins fact meant D6's corpus-skip (LT-59) only ever protected a single host per multi-host recon run. The ONE deliberately breaking (non-additive) rename in this schema's history so far: agreed, since there is no real external MCP consumer of the old singular shape yet (docs/16-implementation-plan-ph7.md's own precedent for an agreed breaking change, the plan tool's tree→{tree,field_suggestions} wrap).
title: ReconResult

target.description: The target URL Run was given.

api_spec.description: Always null in v1 — generic OpenAPI/GraphQL spec parsing is an explicit, named scope cut (docs/14-implementation-plan-ph5.md Step 3's Context section); this field is reserved for a later pass, not yet populated.

signup_endpoint.description: A candidate account-registration endpoint recon found — presence and shape only, like api_spec (Part B, --auto-provision-account). Absent when recon found no candidate.

coupon_endpoint.description: A candidate coupon/promo mint+apply endpoint pair recon found from an OpenAPI spec (LT-135) — real paths and real request-body field names, never invented. Spec-derived only, no path-guess fallback (unlike signup_endpoint): a mint endpoint is POST-only and mutating, so recon never probes for one. Absent when no spec documented a coupon-shaped pair.

secrets.description: Hardcoded secrets found by static analysis of Wave 3's already-fetched JS bodies (Phase 8 Step 3) — a redacted match only, never the real secret value. Empty/absent when nothing was found.

out_of_scope.description: Hosts discovered but excluded per --scope — feeds doc90's B4 scope-creep gate once Phase 6 wires it in.

policy.description: Raw, unparsed policy-relevant artifacts Wave 0 fetches (security.txt body, robots.txt disallow-all) — input to pkg/preflight's D2 pre-flight check (doc15 Step 3). Advisory only; never a block on its own.

uniform_responses.description: One entry per host Wave 3 found answers effectively every request with one generic page rather than routing — a WAF/bot/auth block wall or a SPA/bucket catch-all (Phase 7 Step 4 D6). Empty/absent on a normally-routing run. v1.13 (LT-140): widened from a single nullable `uniform_response` object (first-host-wins) to this array so a second walled host in a multi-host recon run is no longer dropped — a breaking rename, not additive; there is no real external consumer of the old singular shape yet.

app_surface.description: Recon's one-line verdict on whether there is a live application worth planning against, synthesised from uniform_responses, how many endpoints answered 2xx, and whether anything was fingerprinted (docs/follow-up.md LT-68). Additive; absent only on a result produced before v1.5.

warnings.description: Non-fatal degrade notices, e.g. a missing recon binary skipping its wave — inspectable, not just stderr text.

security_txt.description: security.txt body, truncated to a scan-only length; substring-scanned for advisory warnings, never parsed.

body_len.description: Response body length in bytes, as measured by probeCommonPaths' own GET or httpx -cl. Omitted (0) when recon didn't measure it — v1.3, LT-30b.

content_type.description: Response Content-Type (value only, charset param kept as-is), from probeCommonPaths or httpx -ct. Omitted when unmeasured — v1.3, LT-30b.

title.description: HTML <title>, from httpx -title. Omitted when unmeasured — v1.3, LT-30b.

source.description: e.g. "wave0-security-txt", "httpx", "katana-crawl", "wave3-common-path-probe", "wave3-auth-boundary-heuristic", "robots-txt", "sitemap-xml", "api-spec" (routes walked from a reachable OpenAPI/Swagger JSON doc — v1.7, LT-40).

auth_required.description: Set only on a source "api-spec" fact: the OpenAPI document declares this route needs authentication (operation-level `security`, else the doc default). Feeds an authbypass "should reject me" candidate. Omitted/false otherwise — v1.8, LT-90.

redirect_chain.description: One "<status> <url>" line per redirect hop — set only when httpx followed a redirect to a different host (v1.6, LT-64).

final_url.description: Where a cross-host redirect chain landed. status_code stays the first-hop 3xx; the destination's shape/tech are not attributed here (v1.6, LT-64).

body_param_keys.description: Set only on a source "api-spec" fact whose operation has a requestBody JSON schema: the request-body property names the spec declares, names only — no values invented. Feeds SuggestSSRFBodyParamsFromRecon, closing the gap where an attacker-controlled URL is taken in a JSON body field rather than a query string. Omitted otherwise — v1.10, LT-96.

host.description: Which host produced this tech signal — added in v1.1.

url.description: The JS bundle the secret was found in.

redacted.description: First/last few characters only — never the full secret value.

method.description: A spec-derived hint's own documented method, else "POST" (the path-guess fallback's default assumption).

code_field.description: The mint operation's own declared requestBody field name carrying the coupon/voucher code — matched by keyword against the spec's real declared names, never invented.

amount_field.description: The mint operation's own declared requestBody field name carrying the credit/discount amount — matched the same way as code_field.

canary_status.description: HTTP status the guaranteed-nonexistent canary path returned.

blocked_ratio.description: Fraction of this host's Wave 3 probes that came back intercepted (canary-shaped or 401/403/429) — ~1.0 means recon is blind here (LT-62).

verdict.description: "none" = nothing to scan from this vantage (a wall, or no real content and no fingerprint); "thin" = reachable but sparse; "full" = a real mapped surface.

Confidence.description: Mirrors pkg/agenttask.Confidence's string values — not Finding.confidence.
